_doc: HMTc Category 4 (Fruits, Vegetables, and Produce) compiler config for tools/standards/compile-category.mjs. Method v2.0, government-limit-only. Eight taxonomy rows: fresh/frozen fruit, dried fruit, fruit snacks, leafy vegetables other than spinach, spinach, non-root vegetables, root and tuber vegetables, and pickled/fermented/brined vegetables. Produce is the most densely regulated food domain in the register: EU Reg. 2023/915 and its Swiss mirror (VHK 817.022.15), EU Reg. 2024/1987 for nickel, Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2, AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19, MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 with its Paraguayan enactment, and Israel MOH FCS-2016 all publish per-produce-class maximum levels for lead and cadmium, and between them cover total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, total mercury and nickel. Every number in this config is a named register row; no cell is occurrence-derived, and no percentile, occurrence floor, precautionary adjustment or feasibility adjustment is used anywhere. BASIS IS THE LOAD-BEARING DISCIPLINE FOR THIS CATEGORY: the five fresh rows and the drained pickled row sit in a wet-weight edible-portion as-sold basis and take wet-weight, portion-ordinarily-consumed and as-sold maximum levels at face value; dried fruit and manufactured fruit snacks sit in a dry or concentrated as-offered basis and may name ONLY maximum levels written in that basis, enforced mechanically by a basis_guard, because converting a fresh wet-weight maximum level to a dry basis would require an invented reconstitution factor and Method v2.0 confines reconstitution conversion to infant formula. STAFF / HMTc content, not public wiki (CLAUDE.md Part 19 firewall).

_category.name: Fruits, Vegetables, and Produce
_category.anchor: Per-produce-class sovereign maximum levels for lead and cadmium (EU Reg. 2023/915 and Switzerland VHK 817.022.15; Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2; AU-NZ Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016), nickel under EU Reg. 2024/1987, total and inorganic arsenic under MERCOSUR and Israel MOH FCS-2016, and total mercury under Hong Kong Cap. 132V and Israel MOH FCS-2016.
_category.basis_family: dietary as-sold; fresh and frozen produce and drained pickled product on a wet-weight edible-portion basis, dried fruit and manufactured fruit snacks on a dry or concentrated as-offered basis that is never conflated with the fresh wet-weight maximum levels
_category.method_label: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only; the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for the row's product form in the row's native basis, a disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination, or a control; never occurrence-derived)
_category.method_note: CELL RESOLUTION RULE, applied uniformly across all eight rows. (R1) Where a credible sovereign government writes a maximum level for this product form in this row's native basis, the cell is the strictest such value and is tagged regulatory-alignment. (R2) Where the exact cell is unregulated but a credible sovereign writes a maximum level for the SAME commodity in an adjacent form or basis, the cell is a disclosed read-across from that named row, taken at face value only where face value is the conservative (stricter) direction. (R3) Where no sovereign instrument reaches the commodity at all, the cell is a CONTROL: testing is mandatory, an escalation rule is published, and no number is invented. Aluminium is a control in all eight rows because no jurisdiction regulates aluminium as a produce contaminant. Hexavalent chromium is a substantiated not-material determination wherever a total-chromium parent is published for the row and a control wherever it is not; it is never a published number. Methylmercury is a substantiated not-material determination in all eight rows, bounded by the published total-mercury ceiling, because terrestrial produce has no aquatic methylation compartment. TAXONOMY LUMPING IS DISCLOSED, NOT SILENTLY RESOLVED: several sovereign instruments split classes that this taxonomy carries as a single row (fruiting versus bulb versus brassica versus legume vegetables inside non-root-vegetables; temperate versus tropical roots and tubers inside root-tuber-vegetables; table olives versus pickled cucumbers versus fermented brassicas inside pickled-fermented-vegetables; pome, stone, citrus and berry fruit inside fresh-fruit). Because one published HMTc value must be met by every product in the row, each such row binds the strictest value applicable to any member, which is materially stricter than law for the looser members. Every collapsed split is named in that row's scope_note, and the recommended taxonomy splits are recorded as outstanding items rather than resolved by picking a looser residual-class value, which would let HMTc certify a lot that is unlawful in a market of sale.
_category.credible_note: The default credible-regulator set is widened by four members for this category, each of which contributes a comprehensive per-commodity produce contaminant schedule rather than a single opportune entry, and each of which is already treated as credible by the live Category 27, 28 and 29 plant-commodity compilers. Switzerland (VHK 817.022.15, 218 register rows) is an EU-aligned metal and metalloid annex whose per-class produce values mirror EU Reg. 2023/915 and EU Reg. 2024/1987 and which supplies the per-class cadmium and nickel rows that are absent from the register's EU coverage. MERCOSUR (GMC Res. 12/2011, 159 rows) is a supranational bloc instrument with a complete produce schedule for lead, cadmium and total arsenic on a product-as-offered-to-consumer basis, including the only dried-fruit and table-olive rows in the register; Paraguay (Decreto 1335/2019, 159 rows) is its national enactment at identical values and is admitted so the audit scan sees the national instrument as well as the bloc resolution. Israel (MOH FCS-2016, 166 rows) supplies the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables and the only total-mercury and inorganic-arsenic rows for dried fruit. Every anchor in this config remains inside this set, and the audit scan runs across all twelve members. Regulators present in the register but NOT admitted here (China, Thailand, India, Vietnam, Singapore, GSO, Colombia, Panama, Uruguay, Trinidad and Tobago, Philippines, Morocco, Fiji) are not a judgment about their credibility; admitting them is a separate governance decision, and China GB 2762 in particular has no produce rows in the register at all (recorded as a register gap).

fresh-fruit.name: Fresh and frozen fruit
fresh-fruit.native_basis_label: fresh or frozen fruit as sold, wet weight, edible portion after washing and removal of stones, stems and inedible peel
fresh-fruit.scope_note: Whole and cut fresh fruit and individually quick-frozen fruit: pome fruit, stone fruit, citrus, berries and small fruit, grapes, tropical and subtropical fruit, and melons. Freezing does not change the water content materially, so frozen fruit shares the fresh wet-weight basis. OUT OF SCOPE: dried and dehydrated fruit (dried-fruit row, a different basis); fruit snacks, purees, leathers, jams and compotes (fruit-snacks row); fruit juices, nectars and fruit drinks (Category 5 Beverages); canned fruit in hermetically sealed tinplate (Category 7 canned-foods-general, which carries the tin maximum level); table olives (pickled-fermented-vegetables row); fruiting vegetables such as tomato, pepper, aubergine and cucurbits, which are botanically fruits but which every sovereign schedule classes as fruiting vegetables (non-root-vegetables row); tree nuts and dried pulses (Categories 28 and 27); products marketed for ages 0 to 5, which route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule. COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLITS: the sovereign schedules split this row for lead (Hong Kong, Switzerland and MERCOSUR set 200 ug/kg for cranberries, currants, elderberries and strawberry-tree fruit against 100 ug/kg for other fruit) and for cadmium (Switzerland sets 20 ug/kg for pome, stone and citrus fruit, 30 ug/kg for berries and small fruit, 40 ug/kg for raspberries and 50 ug/kg for other fruit). The row binds the strictest member value in each case, so berry and cranberry products certify against a bar stricter than their own sovereign class value.
fresh-fruit.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
fresh-fruit.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row.

Pb.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
Pb.label: Five independent credible regulators converge on 100 ug/kg lead for fresh fruit (Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9, AU-NZ Schedule 19, Switzerland VHK Obst, MERCOSUR GMC 12/2011 with Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019, Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3); the berry carve-outs at 200 ug/kg are named so the collapsed split is visible.
Pb.substantiation: Direct maximum levels for the exact product form in the row's native basis. The berry and cranberry rows at 200 ug/kg are the government-written carve-outs for the accumulating small-fruit species; because one HMTc value must hold across the whole row, the row binds 100 ug/kg and cranberry, currant and elderberry products certify against a value stricter than their own sovereign class. The AU-NZ row is applied on the fresh basis only; Schedule 19 calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis, which is why it is not carried into the dried-fruit row. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS (from the broader register review rather than this row's scan, which returned no stricter-unselected rows): two stricter Hong Kong rows exist that are not applicable to fresh fruit. 'Tomatoes, preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed' (50 ug/kg) is a heat-sterilised canned tomato product and routes to Category 32 tomato-condiments. 'Canned chestnuts and canned chestnuts puree' (50 ug/kg) is a canned tree-nut product and routes to Category 28. MERCOSUR's 'fruit-based ice cream' rows (lead 70, cadmium 50, total arsenic 100) are a frozen dessert form and are not fresh fruit; no frozen-dessert row exists anywhere in the taxonomy, which is recorded as a taxonomy gap.

Cd.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
Cd.label: Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 sets 20 ug/kg cadmium for pome fruit, stone fruit, citrus fruit and mango, the strictest sovereign cadmium maximum level applicable to any product in this row; MERCOSUR, Paraguay and Israel set 50 ug/kg for fresh fruit generally.
Cd.substantiation: The Swiss annex mirrors EU Reg. 2023/915 and carries the per-class cadmium rows that the register's EU coverage lacks. Pome, stone and citrus fruit are the largest members of this row by volume, so 20 ug/kg is not a marginal member value. Berries at 30 ug/kg, raspberries at 40 ug/kg and residual fruit at 50 ug/kg are the government-written splits; the row binds the strictest, and those looser classes certify against a stricter bar.

tAs.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for fresh fruit, berries and small fruit at 300 ug/kg; Israel MOH FCS-2016 sets 1000 ug/kg for the same commodity class.
tAs.substantiation: Direct total-arsenic maximum levels for fresh fruit in an as-offered basis. Total arsenic is reported for its own sake and is never satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell; the inorganic-arsenic species limit for this row (60 ug/kg) is far stricter and is the operative arsenic constraint.

iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables (60 ug/kg); the EU, Codex, FDA, AU-NZ, Hong Kong and Swiss instruments set inorganic-arsenic maximum levels only for rice, juices, seaweed and infant food.
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant arsenic species and is never satisfied by the total-arsenic cell; both are reported. This value is a direct maximum level for the product class, not a read-across, and it sits well below the total-arsenic ceiling for the same row, so the species cell is the binding arsenic constraint in practice.

tHg.basis_label: wet weight, fresh fruit as sold
tHg.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets total mercury for fruits and vegetables at 30 ug/kg, the only sovereign total-mercury maximum level whose scope reaches fresh fruit.
tHg.substantiation: Direct maximum level for the commodity class. Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 sets a stricter 10 ug/kg but its scope is 'vegetables, other than edible fungi' and does not reach fruit, so it is not applicable to this row; it binds the four vegetable rows and the pickled row instead.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form: the routed corpus reports no methylmercury measurement in this matrix, and the only credible methylmercury maximum levels in force (US FDA CPG 540.600; HK Cap. 132V item 11) are scoped to fish, shellfish and crustaceans, so neither supplies an applicable ceiling for a fruit. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury). No methylmercury ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for fruit. EU Reg. 2024/1987, the only comprehensive dietary nickel instrument in existence, enumerates leafy, fruiting, brassica, root, tuber, bulb and legume vegetables, fresh herbs, cereals, pseudocereals, pulses, tree nuts, seeds, cocoa, seaweed and juices, and deliberately sets no maximum level for fruit; the Swiss VHK nickel rows mirror it and likewise omit fruit. Because no instrument reaches the commodity at all, HMTc publishes no nickel number for fresh fruit rather than borrowing the fruiting-vegetable value of 400 ug/kg from a different commodity class.
control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel. Investigate any result above 400 ug/kg (the EU fruiting-vegetable maximum level, used here only as an investigation trigger and not as a certification ceiling) against orchard soil, foliar-spray and stainless-steel processing provenance before release.

not_material.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. Fresh and frozen fruit is sold loose, in fibre punnets, in film or in polymer trays. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.
not_material.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel; a result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source in harvest, wash, transport or packing before the lot is released.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for non-canned produce; all tin maximum levels in the register are conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and the EU rows expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from even that scope.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for this product form. The only dietary total-chromium maximum levels in the register are Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables (500 ug/kg) and pulses, cereals, meat, fish and dairy powder rows under the same item, plus drinking-water and color-additive specifications. The Hong Kong vegetable row does not reach fruit, and no jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for fruit. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone total-chromium number for this row; total chromium is screened on every lot and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated result against soil, irrigation water and processing-equipment provenance and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction, and this row has no published total-chromium parent to bound the species against (the only total-chromium food maximum level in the register, Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, is scoped to vegetables and does not reach this product form). With neither a species limit nor a published parent, HMTc publishes no hexavalent-chromium number and controls the species by mandatory reflex speciation.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.
control.bounded_by: Cr (total chromium, itself a control for this row)

dried-fruit.name: Dried fruit
dried-fruit.native_basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer, dry as-sold basis, no reconstitution conversion applied
dried-fruit.scope_note: Sun-dried, tunnel-dried, osmotically dried, freeze-dried and vacuum-dried whole or cut fruit sold as such: raisins and sultanas, prunes, dried apricots, figs, dates, dried apples, dried mango and papaya, dried cranberries and cherries, and freeze-dried fruit pieces. Water content is roughly 15 to 25 percent against 80 to 90 percent for the fresh commodity, so a fresh wet-weight maximum level is between four and six times stricter than its own intent when applied to this row at face value. THE BASIS IS THE CONTROLLING FACT FOR THIS ROW. Only maximum levels written for the dried commodity on an as-offered or as-placed-on-market basis are named, enforced by the basis_guard. AU-NZ Schedule 19 is expressly excluded even though its fruit lead maximum level of 100 ug/kg is far stricter than the binding value, because Schedule 19 calculates dried and dehydrated foods on the pre-drying basis and is therefore a fresh-equivalent number rather than a dry as-sold number. OUT OF SCOPE: dried leafy vegetables, dried herbs and dried spices (Category 34); dried mushrooms (Category 29); fruit leathers, strips, purees, gummies and other manufactured fruit confections (fruit-snacks row); dried pulses, nuts and seeds (Categories 27 and 28); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1).
dried-fruit.audit_scope: dried fruit|dried fruits|dried vegetables and fruits|trockenfr|getrocknete fr|raisin|sultana|prune|dried apricot|\bdate|\bfig\b
dried-fruit.basis_guard: product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market
dried-fruit.basis_guard_note: This row is a concentrated product in a dry or as-offered basis, so the guard admits only maximum levels expressed for the product as offered to the consumer or as placed on the market and rejects every fresh wet-weight and portion-ordinarily-consumed maximum level. That is deliberate: applying a fresh wet-weight value at face value to a dried product would silently mix bases, and converting between them would require an invented reconstitution factor, which Method v2.0 confines to infant formula.

Pb.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
Pb.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and its Paraguayan enactment Decreto 1335/2019 set lead for dried fruits at 800 ug/kg on a product-as-offered-to-consumer basis, the only sovereign lead maximum level written for this exact cell in this exact basis.
Pb.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level. The value is looser than the 100 ug/kg fresh-fruit lead ceiling and that is the honest arithmetic of the basis, not a concession: a lawful fresh grape at 100 ug/kg becomes a raisin at roughly 400 ug/kg on the dry basis, so a 100 ug/kg dried-fruit ceiling would be a number manufactured by a basis error rather than one compelled by any instrument. Stricter fruit lead maximum levels exist (Hong Kong, AU-NZ, Switzerland, MERCOSUR and Israel all set 100 ug/kg for fresh fruit) and are deliberately not carried across the basis change; the basis_guard makes that mechanical.

read_across.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 writes dried-fruit maximum levels for lead and total arsenic but none for cadmium, so the exact cell is unregulated; the nearest applicable sovereign value is the same instrument's fresh-fruit cadmium maximum level of 50 ug/kg for the same commodity, applied at face value to the dry product.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across within one instrument and one commodity. Face value is the conservative direction here: holding a product with roughly one fifth the water content of the fresh commodity to the fresh cadmium ceiling is approximately five times stricter in fresh-equivalent terms, so the read-across cannot understate contamination. No dry-basis cadmium maximum level for dried fruit exists in any credible jurisdiction, and Israel MOH FCS-2016 lists dried fruits as a separate category (3.1) without a cadmium entry, so its 50 ug/kg general fruits-and-vegetables cadmium row cannot be assumed to reach the dried product and is not relied on.

Cd.basis_label: MERCOSUR fresh-fruit cadmium maximum level applied at face value to the dried product as offered (conservative direction, disclosed)

tAs.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for dried fruits at 800 ug/kg; Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets 5000 ug/kg for dried fruits and vegetables.
tAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum levels for the dried commodity in the dry as-sold basis. MERCOSUR binds. The inorganic-arsenic species limit for this row (300 ug/kg) is far stricter and is the operative arsenic constraint; total arsenic is reported for its own sake and is never satisfied by the species cell.

iAs.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets inorganic arsenic for dried fruits and vegetables at 300 ug/kg, the only sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level written for a dried produce commodity.
iAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level for the dried commodity in the dry as-sold basis. Israel's fresh fruits-and-vegetables inorganic-arsenic row (60 ug/kg) is stricter but sits in the fresh basis and is a different category of the same instrument, so the dried row is the applicable cell; the instrument's own five-fold step between them is the regulator's basis treatment, not an HMTc adjustment.

tHg.basis_label: dried fruit as offered to the consumer (dry as-sold)
tHg.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1 sets total mercury for dried fruits and vegetables at 150 ug/kg, the only sovereign total-mercury maximum level written for a dried produce commodity.
tHg.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level in the dry as-sold basis. The same instrument's fresh row is 30 ug/kg; the five-fold step between the fresh and dried categories is the regulator's own basis treatment and is exactly why the fresh value is not carried into this row.

not_material.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or other terrestrial plant food in any jurisdiction; every methylmercury maximum level in the register is scoped to fish, shellfish and other aquatic animals, where microbial methylation in sediment and water is the documented pathway. Field-grown produce has no aquatic methylation compartment, and mercury taken up by root and leaf tissue is predominantly inorganic Hg(II). Methylmercury is therefore a component of, and bounded by, the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3.1, 150 ug/kg), and no separate methylmercury number is published.
not_material.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury maximum level for produce; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for aquatic species (HK Cap. 132V item 11; US FDA CPG 540.600). Total mercury for this row is published and bounds the species.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for fruit in any form, dried or fresh. EU Reg. 2024/1987 enumerates vegetable, cereal, pulse, nut, seed, cocoa, seaweed and juice classes and sets no fruit maximum level at all, and the Swiss VHK nickel rows mirror it. There is therefore no same-commodity value to read across from, and a vegetable wet-weight nickel maximum level could not be carried into this row's dry as-sold basis in any event. HMTc publishes no nickel number for dried fruit.
control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every lot. Investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own dried-fruit lot history, with attention to stainless-steel dicing and dehydrator contact, and record the drying ratio so results can be compared on a fresh-equivalent basis for surveillance.

Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.

not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for non-canned produce; all tin maximum levels in the register are conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and the EU rows expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from even that scope.

The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. The only dietary total-chromium maximum levels in the register are Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables (500 ug/kg) and pulses, cereals, meat, fish and dairy powder rows under the same item, plus drinking-water and color-additive specifications. The Hong Kong vegetable row does not reach fruit, no jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for fruit, and a wet-weight vegetable value could not be carried into this row's dry as-sold basis. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone total-chromium number for this row; total chromium is screened on every lot and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation.

With neither a species limit nor a published parent, HMTc publishes no hexavalent-chromium number and controls the species by mandatory reflex speciation.

fruit-snacks.name: Fruit snacks
fruit-snacks.native_basis_label: manufactured fruit snack as offered to the consumer, as-sold basis across a wide moisture range (roughly 15 percent for a fruit leather to 80 percent for a puree pouch)
fruit-snacks.scope_note: Manufactured fruit-based snack and spread forms: fruit leathers, strips and rolls, fruit bars whose predominant ingredient is fruit, fruit-puree pouches and cups, fruit gummies and chews formulated from fruit puree or concentrate, and compotes, jellies, jams and marmalades. Products whose predominant ingredient is grain, dairy, nut or confectionery sugar rather than fruit route out (Category 7 snacks-general, Category 33 confectionery, Category 3 grains). Fruit-based ice cream and other frozen dairy desserts route to Category 24. Fruit juices and nectars route to Category 5. Products marketed for ages 0 to 5, including infant and toddler fruit purees and pouches, route to Category 1 by the taxonomy boundary rule, which removes the largest single fruit-puree market from this row. THE ROW'S MOISTURE RANGE IS WHY ONLY AS-OFFERED MAXIMUM LEVELS ARE NAMED: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 writes a maximum level for exactly this product class (compotes, jellies, jams, marmalades and other fruit or vegetable sweets) on a product-as-offered-to-consumer basis, and that instrument governs lead and total arsenic here. Where MERCOSUR is silent, the cell reads across from a same-commodity fresh fruit-and-vegetable maximum level at face value, which is conservative for the concentrated members of the row and approximately basis-matched for the puree members.
fruit-snacks.audit_scope: jam|jell|marmalade|compote|fruit or vegetable sweet|fruit sweet|fruit snack|fruit leather|fruit bar|fruit pur[eé]e|fruit puree|fruit-based ice cream|fruit based ice cream
fruit-snacks.basis_guard: product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market
fruit-snacks.basis_guard_note: This row is a concentrated product in a dry or as-offered basis, so the guard admits only maximum levels expressed for the product as offered to the consumer or as placed on the market and rejects every fresh wet-weight and portion-ordinarily-consumed maximum level. That is deliberate: applying a fresh wet-weight value at face value to a dried product would silently mix bases, and converting between them would require an invented reconstitution factor, which Method v2.0 confines to infant formula.

Pb.basis_label: manufactured fruit snack as offered to the consumer
Pb.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set lead at 200 ug/kg for compotes, jellies, jams, marmalades and other fruit or vegetable sweets, the sovereign class that this taxonomy row names as fruit snacks, on a product-as-offered-to-consumer basis.
Pb.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level for the manufactured product class in the row's own basis. Fresh-fruit lead maximum levels of 100 ug/kg exist in five jurisdictions and are not carried into this row: the row spans moisture contents from 15 to 80 percent, so no single fresh wet-weight value can be applied to it without an invented basis conversion, and MERCOSUR's own decision to write a separate looser value for fruit sweets is the regulator's treatment of that same concentration effect. Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9 independently writes a maximum level for jams, jellies and marmalades at 400 ug/kg, which corroborates that sovereign regulators treat this product class as its own cell rather than as fresh fruit, but it is deliberately NOT named as an anchor: Cap 132V expresses every value on a single 'food as listed in the Schedule' basis that the register cannot distinguish from the fresh wet-weight as-sold rows of the same instrument, so it fails this row's basis guard. Naming it produced a hard compile failure, which is the guard performing its function; it is cited here as corroboration only, and it is looser than the binding value in any case. AUDIT DISPOSITIONS: the scan surfaces MERCOSUR and Paraguay 'fruit-based ice cream' at 70 ug/kg, which is a frozen dessert rather than a fruit snack (no frozen-dessert row exists anywhere in the taxonomy, recorded as a taxonomy gap), The broader register review additionally surfaces Hong Kong 'Canned chestnuts and canned chestnuts puree' at 50 ug/kg, a canned tree-nut product routing to Category 28; it was matched only by an over-broad 'puree' token in an earlier draft of this row's audit_scope, which has been narrowed to 'fruit puree' so the scan no longer reports a false positive.

read_across.label: MERCOSUR writes no cadmium maximum level for fruit sweets, so the exact cell is unregulated; the nearest applicable sovereign value is the same instrument's fresh-fruit cadmium maximum level of 50 ug/kg for the same commodity, applied at face value.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across within one instrument and one commodity. Face value is conservative for the concentrated members of the row (a fruit leather held to the fresh-fruit ceiling is several times stricter in fresh-equivalent terms) and approximately basis-matched for the puree members, so the read-across cannot understate contamination in either direction.

Cd.basis_label: MERCOSUR fresh-fruit cadmium maximum level applied at face value to the manufactured snack as offered (conservative direction, disclosed)

tAs.basis_label: manufactured fruit snack as offered to the consumer
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic at 300 ug/kg for compotes, jellies, jams, marmalades and other fruit or vegetable sweets.
tAs.substantiation: R1 direct maximum level for the manufactured product class in the row's own basis. Total arsenic is never satisfied by the inorganic-arsenic cell; both are reported. AUDIT DISPOSITION: the scan surfaces MERCOSUR and Paraguay 'fruit-based ice cream' total arsenic at 100 ug/kg, a frozen dessert form outside this row.

read_across.label: No jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for manufactured fruit snacks; the nearest applicable sovereign value is Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 for fruits and vegetables, 60 ug/kg, the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for this commodity.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity. Israel writes a separate dried-produce inorganic-arsenic row at 300 ug/kg; the fresh row is named instead because it is the conservative direction and because this row's moisture range straddles both categories, so choosing the looser dried value would be selecting for convenience rather than for applicability. Inorganic arsenic never satisfies the total-arsenic cell.

iAs.basis_label: Israel fresh fruits-and-vegetables inorganic-arsenic maximum level applied at face value to the manufactured snack as offered (conservative direction, disclosed)

read_across.label: No jurisdiction sets a total-mercury maximum level for manufactured fruit snacks; the nearest applicable sovereign value is Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 for fruits and vegetables, 30 ug/kg.
read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity, conservative direction. The same instrument's dried-produce total-mercury row is 150 ug/kg; the fresh row is named because it is the stricter of the two applicable categories and this row straddles both.

tHg.basis_label: Israel fresh fruits-and-vegetables total-mercury maximum level applied at face value to the manufactured snack as offered (conservative direction, disclosed)

not_material.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or other terrestrial plant food in any jurisdiction; every methylmercury maximum level in the register is scoped to fish, shellfish and other aquatic animals, where microbial methylation in sediment and water is the documented pathway. Field-grown produce has no aquatic methylation compartment, and mercury taken up by root and leaf tissue is predominantly inorganic Hg(II). Methylmercury is therefore a component of, and bounded by, the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (read-across from Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3, 30 ug/kg), and no separate methylmercury number is published.
not_material.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a methylmercury maximum level for produce; methylmercury maximum levels exist only for aquatic species (HK Cap. 132V item 11; US FDA CPG 540.600). Total mercury for this row is published and bounds the species.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a nickel maximum level for fruit in any form or for manufactured fruit snacks. EU Reg. 2024/1987 enumerates vegetable, cereal, pulse, nut, seed, cocoa, seaweed and juice classes and writes no fruit maximum level, so there is no same-commodity value to read across from. HMTc publishes no nickel number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total nickel by ICP-MS on every lot. Investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history, with attention to stainless-steel evaporator, extruder and depositor contact, which is the plausible process source in this row.

control.rationale: Tin in this row is a packaging-migration analyte rather than a property of the food. Every sovereign tin maximum level in the register is conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and fruit snacks are a manufactured packaged form in which a hermetically sealed tinplate or metal-lined presentation cannot be excluded across the row (jams and compotes in particular are still packed in cans in some markets), while leathers, pouches, cups and gummies have no tinplate contact at all. Because the row's presentation determines whether any sovereign tin limit applies at all, HMTc publishes no standalone tin number for the row and instead makes the screen mandatory with an escalation to the canned-foods maximum level whenever the certified presentation is tinplate.
control.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot. Where the certified presentation is a tinplate can or a metal-lined closure, the canned-foods maximum level (EU Reg. 2023/915, 200000 ug/kg) applies as a regulatory hard stop and the lot is additionally tested at end of shelf life; where the presentation is glass, pouch or plastic, any result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a total-chromium maximum level for this product form. The only dietary total-chromium maximum levels in the register are Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 for vegetables (500 ug/kg) and pulses, cereals, meat, fish and dairy powder rows under the same item, plus drinking-water and color-additive specifications. The Hong Kong vegetable row does not reach fruit or manufactured fruit snacks, and no jurisdiction writes a total-chromium maximum level for either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone total-chromium number for this row; total chromium is screened on every lot and hexavalent chromium is controlled by reflex speciation.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot; investigate any elevated result against soil, irrigation water and processing-equipment provenance and reflex-speciate per the Cr-VI control.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction, and this row has no published total-chromium parent to bound the species against (the only total-chromium food maximum level in the register, Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, is scoped to vegetables and does not reach this product form). With neither a species limit nor a published parent, HMTc publishes no hexavalent-chromium number and controls the species by mandatory reflex speciation.
control.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.
control.bounded_by: Cr (total chromium, itself a control for this row)

leafy-vegetables-other.name: Leafy and green vegetables other than spinach
leafy-vegetables-other.native_basis_label: fresh or frozen leafy vegetable as sold, wet weight, edible portion after washing and separation of the edible part
leafy-vegetables-other.scope_note: Leaf vegetables and leafy brassicas other than spinach: lettuce and other salad leaves, rocket, chicory, endive, escarole, chard, watercress, lamb's lettuce, and the leafy brassicas (kale, collards, pak choi, Chinese cabbage, mustard greens). Frozen leaf vegetables share the fresh wet-weight basis. THE SPINACH SPLIT IS REAL AND PRESERVED: spinach and similar leaves are excluded here and carry their own row, because EU Reg. 2023/915, Switzerland VHK, Hong Kong Cap. 132V, MERCOSUR and Israel all write spinach out of the general leaf-vegetable class. THE BRASSICA SPLIT IS ALSO A GOVERNMENT SPLIT AND IS HONOURED IN THE SCOPING: head and flowering brassicas (cabbage heads, broccoli, cauliflower, kohlrabi, Brussels sprouts) are NOT in this row; they route to non-root-vegetables, matching Hong Kong's division between 'leafy vegetables including Brassica leafy vegetables' and 'Brassica vegetables other than Brassica leafy vegetables', and Switzerland's division between Blattkohle (leaf cabbages, cadmium 100 ug/kg) and Kohlgemüse (head and flowering brassicas, cadmium 40 ug/kg, expressly excluding Blattkohle). OUT OF SCOPE: fresh culinary herbs and dried herbs and seasonings (Category 34, which is also why the EU and Swiss leaf-vegetable rows named here carry their own 'except fresh herbs' carve-out); edible fungi (Category 29); seaweed and kelp (Category 6); sprouts and microgreens sold as such; dried leafy vegetables (Category 34); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1). COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLIT: for lead, AU-NZ Schedule 19 sets 100 ug/kg for vegetables except brassicas and 300 ug/kg for brassicas, so the non-brassica members of this row are held to 100 ug/kg by Australian and New Zealand law while the leafy-brassica members are not. The row binds 100 ug/kg, which is stricter than any instrument applies to kale or pak choi.
leafy-vegetables-other.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
leafy-vegetables-other.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row.

Pb.basis_label: wet weight, fresh leafy vegetable as sold
Pb.label: AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19 sets lead at 100 ug/kg for vegetables except brassicas, which as a matter of Australian and New Zealand law caps lettuce, rocket, chard and every other non-brassica leaf vegetable in this row; the EU, Swiss, Hong Kong, MERCOSUR, Paraguayan and Israeli leaf-vegetable rows all sit at 300 ug/kg.
Pb.substantiation: The 100 ug/kg value is a direct maximum level applicable to the majority of this row by species count and by volume. It is selected because a published HMTc value of 300 ug/kg would certify a lettuce lot at 250 ug/kg that is unlawful in Australia and New Zealand, which is the failure mode the government-limit method exists to prevent. The consequence is disclosed rather than hidden: the leafy-brassica members of the row (kale, pak choi, collards) are held to a value three times stricter than the 300 ug/kg that AU-NZ, the EU, Switzerland, Hong Kong, MERCOSUR and Israel all apply to them, and the recommended taxonomy fix is a separate leafy-brassica row.

Cd.basis_label: wet weight, fresh leafy vegetable as sold
Cd.label: EU Reg. 2023/915, its Swiss mirror (Blattgemüse and Blattkohle) and AU-NZ Schedule 19 all set cadmium for leaf vegetables at 100 ug/kg; Hong Kong, MERCOSUR, Paraguay and Israel set 200 ug/kg for the same class.
Cd.substantiation: Four-instrument convergence on 100 ug/kg as a direct maximum level for the exact product form in the row's native basis. The Swiss Kohlgemüse cadmium row at 40 ug/kg is not named because its own text excludes Blattkohle, so it does not reach the leafy brassicas in this row; it binds the non-root-vegetables row instead, where the head and flowering brassicas sit. AUDIT DISPOSITION: the scan surfaces Hong Kong 'Brassica vegetables, other than Brassica leafy vegetables' cadmium at 50 ug/kg, matched only because the phrase 'Brassica leafy vegetables' appears inside its own exclusion clause. That row expressly excludes the leafy brassicas that are the only brassicas in this row, so it is not applicable here; it binds the non-root-vegetables row.

tAs.basis_label: wet weight, fresh leafy vegetable as sold
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for leaf vegetables at 300 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 2 sets 500 ug/kg for vegetables and Israel MOH FCS-2016 sets 1000 ug/kg.
tAs.substantiation: Direct maximum levels for the leaf-vegetable class. The inorganic-arsenic species limit for this row (60 ug/kg) is far stricter and is the operative arsenic constraint; total arsenic is reported for its own sake.

iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables (60 ug/kg); the EU, Codex, FDA, AU-NZ, Hong Kong and Swiss instruments set inorganic-arsenic maximum levels only for rice, juices, seaweed and infant food.
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant arsenic species and is never satisfied by the total-arsenic cell; both are reported. This value is a direct maximum level for the product class, not a read-across, and it sits well below the total-arsenic ceiling for the same row, so the species cell is the binding arsenic constraint in practice.

tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 sets total mercury for vegetables other than edible fungi at 10 ug/kg, the strictest sovereign total-mercury maximum level applicable to this product form; Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets 30 ug/kg for the same commodity class.
tHg.substantiation: Both named rows are direct maximum levels for the vegetable class in an as-sold basis. Hong Kong binds. Edible fungi are expressly outside the Hong Kong row (they carry 100 ug/kg under the same item) and route to Category 29, so the 10 ug/kg value is not being borrowed from a mushroom limit.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for this product form: wang2021-houttuynia-mercury-china measured methylmercury in this matrix, so the species is not absent and no not-material determination is supportable. Methylmercury is therefore held under mandatory analytical control rather than recorded not-material, and it remains bounded by identity below the published total-mercury ceiling for this row (methylmercury cannot exceed total mercury). No methylmercury ceiling is invented.
control.reference_method: Methylmercury by GC-ICP-MS or EN 16801, required only on a lot whose total mercury reaches 60 percent of the published total-mercury ceiling; any quantifiable methylmercury on such a lot is investigated and the lot is held pending root-cause analysis.

Ni.basis_label: wet weight, fresh leafy vegetable as sold
Ni.label: EU Reg. 2024/1987 sets nickel for leafy vegetables except fresh herbs at 500 ug/kg, mirrored by Switzerland VHK Blattgemüse at the same value.
Ni.substantiation: Direct maximum level for the exact product form in the row's native basis, from the only comprehensive dietary nickel instrument in existence. Fresh herbs carry a separate 1200 ug/kg nickel row and route to Category 34, so this row is not borrowing the herb allowance.

not_material.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. Fresh and frozen leafy vegetables are sold loose, bagged or in polymer clamshells. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.
not_material.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel; a result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source in harvest, wash, transport or packing before the lot is released.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a tin maximum level for non-canned produce; all tin maximum levels in the register are conditioned on a canned (tinplate) presentation, and the EU rows expressly exclude canned dried and canned powdered products from even that scope.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective ceiling. Dietary chromium is dominated by nutritionally essential Cr(III); the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), which is controlled separately by reflex speciation. A lot may satisfy this screen and still fail on Cr(VI), and the screen is excluded from the firm-limit count.
Cr.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7 sets total chromium for vegetables other than pulses at 500 ug/kg, the only dietary total-chromium maximum level any credible government writes for this product form.
Cr.substantiation: Named as the sovereign total-chromium value for the vegetable class in its as-sold basis. Pulses are expressly outside this row (1000 ug/kg under the same item) and route to Category 27. Total chromium never satisfies the Cr(VI) cell.

not_material.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction; every Cr(VI) limit in the register governs articles and materials (toys, textiles, leather, fertilisers, electrical equipment), not diet. Chromium in produce is dominated by nutritionally essential Cr(III), and Cr(VI) is not stable in the plant matrix: fruit and vegetable tissue is an aqueous, organic-acid and ascorbate-rich reducing medium in which Cr(VI) is reduced to Cr(III), so a reported Cr(VI) value in this matrix reflects extraction conditions rather than the chromium species the consumer ingests. Hexavalent chromium is therefore bounded by the published total-chromium screen for this row (Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 7, 500 ug/kg) and controlled by reflex speciation rather than by a published number.
not_material.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot. Cr(VI) is never published as a panel number.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No jurisdiction sets a dietary Cr(VI) maximum level; the register's Cr(VI) rows are article and material limits (EU 2009/48 toys, EU 2018/1513 textiles, EU 301/2014 leather, EU 2019/1009 fertilisers, EU RoHS). The total-chromium parent for this row is published.
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU Reg. 2023/915; EU Reg. 2024/1987 (nickel); Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 (2026 metal/metalloid annex); Hong Kong Cap. 132V Part 2 Schedule; AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019; Israel MOH FCS-2016; Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR, action levels)

spinach.name: Spinach and similar leaves
spinach.native_basis_label: fresh or frozen spinach as sold, wet weight, edible portion after washing and separation of the edible part
spinach.scope_note: Spinach (Spinacia oleracea) and the similar-leaf species that sovereign schedules group with it, plus mustard seedlings, in fresh, baby-leaf and frozen form. This row exists because the sovereign rules split it: EU Reg. 2023/915 writes spinach out of the general leaf-vegetable cadmium row (100 ug/kg) into its own row at 200 ug/kg, Switzerland mirrors that split exactly (Blattgemüse 100 excluding Spinat; Spinat und verwandte Arten 200), and Hong Kong, Thailand, India, Vietnam and Panama all write 'other than spinach' into their leafy-vegetable lead rows. Frozen spinach shares the fresh wet-weight basis; spinach puree, creamed spinach and other prepared forms route to Category 35, and dried spinach powder routes to Category 34. Products marketed for ages 0 to 5 route to Category 1. THE CADMIUM CELL IS THE ONE A HOSTILE EXPERT WILL READ FIRST, so it is argued in full in that cell's substantiation.
spinach.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
spinach.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row.

Pb.basis_label: wet weight, fresh spinach as sold
Pb.label: AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19 sets lead at 100 ug/kg for vegetables except brassicas, which covers spinach as a matter of Australian and New Zealand law; the EU leaf-vegetable row (whose scope note records that it covers spinach), its Swiss mirror, MERCOSUR, Paraguay and Israel all sit at 300 ug/kg.
Pb.substantiation: Spinach is not a brassica, so the AU-NZ 100 ug/kg row applies to it directly with no interpretation. It is the strictest applicable sovereign lead maximum level for this exact product form and is selected on that basis. Hong Kong's leafy-vegetable lead row is expressly 'other than spinach' and is therefore not applicable to this row and is not named.

Cd.basis_label: wet weight, fresh spinach as sold
Cd.label: AU-NZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19 sets cadmium at 100 ug/kg for leafy vegetables with no spinach carve-out, which caps spinach in Australia and New Zealand; the EU spinach row, its Swiss mirror, Hong Kong, MERCOSUR, Paraguay and Israel all sit at 200 ug/kg.
Cd.substantiation: This is the cell where the instruments genuinely disagree, so the reasoning is stated in full. The EU wrote spinach out of the 100 ug/kg leaf-vegetable row into a 200 ug/kg row precisely because spinach accumulates more cadmium than other leaves, and Switzerland, Hong Kong, MERCOSUR and Israel are at 200 ug/kg as well. AU-NZ Schedule 19 has no spinach carve-out: its cadmium entry is 'leafy vegetables 0.1 mg/kg', which caps spinach sold in Australia and New Zealand at 100 ug/kg. HMTc binds 100 ug/kg. Achievability is deliberately not an input to this selection, because feasibility-selected numeric rationales are retired under Method v2.0; the only question the method asks is which applicable sovereign maximum level is strictest, and a published value of 200 ug/kg would certify spinach lots that are unlawful in two of the twelve credible jurisdictions. The gap between the EU and AU-NZ treatments is stated, not hidden, and no occurrence evidence was consulted in choosing between them.

tAs.basis_label: wet weight, fresh spinach as sold
tAs.label: MERCOSUR GMC Res. 12/2011 and Paraguay Decreto 1335/2019 set total arsenic for leaf vegetables including loose-leaf brassicas and fresh aromatic herbs at 300 ug/kg; Hong Kong sets 500 ug/kg for vegetables and Israel 1000 ug/kg.
tAs.substantiation: No jurisdiction writes a spinach-specific total-arsenic maximum level, so the general leaf-vegetable rows of each instrument are the applicable cells for this product form. The inorganic-arsenic species limit of 60 ug/kg is the operative arsenic constraint.

iAs.label: Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets the only inorganic-arsenic maximum level any credible government writes for fruits and vegetables (60 ug/kg); the EU, Codex, FDA, AU-NZ, Hong Kong and Swiss instruments set inorganic-arsenic maximum levels only for rice, juices, seaweed and infant food.
iAs.substantiation: Inorganic arsenic is the health-relevant arsenic species and is never satisfied by the total-arsenic cell; both are reported. This value is a direct maximum level for the product class, not a read-across, and it sits well below the total-arsenic ceiling for the same row, so the species cell is the binding arsenic constraint in practice.

tHg.basis_label: wet weight, fresh spinach as sold
tHg.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 12 sets total mercury for vegetables other than edible fungi at 10 ug/kg; Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 3 sets 30 ug/kg for fruits and vegetables.
tHg.substantiation: Hong Kong's vegetable row has no spinach carve-out for mercury and is the strictest applicable sovereign total-mercury maximum level for this product form. Edible fungi are expressly outside it and route to Category 29.

The row binds the strictest applicable value in each cell, so onions, broccoli and green beans certify against fruiting-vegetable values that no government applies to them. This is the row whose taxonomy split is most worth making.

root-tuber-vegetables.name: Root and tuber vegetables

root-tuber-vegetables.scope_note: Fresh and frozen roots and tubers: potato (assessed peeled, as every instrument specifies), sweet potato, carrot, parsnip, beetroot, radish, turnip, swede, celeriac, salsify, parsley root, horseradish, and the tropical roots and tubers (cassava, taro, yam, arrowroot). Frozen and pre-cut forms share the fresh wet-weight basis. This row is a distinct subcategory because roots and tubers take cadmium up from soil differently from leaves and fruits, which is the boundary rule the taxonomy states. OUT OF SCOPE: ginger and turmeric, which the Swiss root-and-tuber lead row expressly excludes and which route to Category 34 as rhizome spices; root-vegetable crisps and chips, which route to Category 7 as a snack form; dried and powdered roots (Category 34); pickled roots such as beetroot and radish (pickled-fermented-vegetables row); root vegetable juices (Category 5); single-ingredient root vegetables marketed for children under 2, which route to Category 1 and carry the FDA 20 ug/kg lead action level there rather than here; canned roots in tinplate (Category 7). COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLIT: Switzerland sets cadmium at 50 ug/kg for tropical roots and tubers and for parsley roots, 100 ug/kg for temperate roots and tubers generally, 150 ug/kg for celeriac and 200 ug/kg for salsify, and its lead row excludes salsify (300 ug/kg). EU Reg. 2023/915, AU-NZ, Hong Kong, MERCOSUR and Israel each set a single 100 ug/kg cadmium value for the whole class. The row binds 50 ug/kg, so potato, carrot and beetroot certify against the value written for the cleaner tropical roots. That is over-compliance rather than a defect, but the split is worth making in the taxonomy and is recorded as an outstanding item.

not_material.rationale: Every tin maximum level in the register is scoped to canned product: EU Reg. 2023/915 sets 200000 ug/kg for canned foods and 100000 ug/kg for canned beverages, Codex CXS 193-1995 and AU-NZ Schedule 19 set 250000 ug/kg for canned foods, and Hong Kong Cap. 132V sets 250000 ug/kg for canned food other than canned beverages. Those limits regulate one contamination pathway, dissolution of tin from tinplate into the packed food. This row is not packed in tinplate, so the pathway that every sovereign tin limit addresses is physically absent and any tin present is dietary background rather than packaging migration. Fresh and frozen roots and tubers are sold loose, netted, bagged or in polymer trays. Hermetically sealed tinplate presentations of this commodity route to the canned-foods row in Category 7 and carry the canned-foods tin maximum level there.
not_material.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every lot as part of the mandatory eight-totals panel; a result above 50 ug/kg is investigated for a metal-contact source in harvest, wash, transport or packing before the lot is released.

control.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets an aluminium contaminant maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or produce form in any jurisdiction. The register's aluminium limits are drinking-water and bottled-water parameters, infant-formula maximum levels, a food-contact plastics specific migration limit, toy migration limits, and permitted-additive levels for baked and starch foods; none of them regulates aluminium as a contaminant of produce. Aluminium is also the third most abundant element in the earth's crust and appears in produce largely as soil-derived and root-associated mineral content rather than as process contamination, so no near-neighbour read-across is supportable either. Under the government-limit-only method HMTc publishes no standalone aluminium number for this row.
control.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every lot, reported to the applicant. Document any aluminium-containing processing aid, packaging contact or anti-caking agent, comply with the additive rules of every market of sale, and investigate any result that is an outlier against the applicant's own lot history.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is recorded as a SCREEN, not a protective ceiling. A lot may satisfy this screen and still fail on Cr(VI), and the screen is excluded from the firm-limit count.

not_material.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a hexavalent-chromium maximum level for any food in any jurisdiction; every Cr(VI) limit in the register governs articles and materials (toys, textiles, leather, fertilisers, electrical equipment), not diet. not_material.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every lot. Any total-chromium result at or above 100 ug/kg triggers Cr(VI) speciation by EN 15192 or EPA 6800 IC-ICP-MS isotope dilution; any quantifiable Cr(VI) at LOQ fails the lot. Cr(VI) is never published as a panel number.

pickled-fermented-vegetables.name: Pickled, fermented and brined vegetables
pickled-fermented-vegetables.native_basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight, brine and packing liquid excluded from the analytical portion
pickled-fermented-vegetables.scope_note: Vegetables preserved by acidification, lactic fermentation or brining and sold as such: cucumber pickles and gherkins, sauerkraut, kimchi, pickled onions, beetroot and radish, giardiniera and mixed pickles, olives cured for table use, and pickled peppers. THE BASIS IS THE DRAINED PRODUCT: brine and packing liquid are excluded from the analytical portion, which matches the AU-NZ 'portion ordinarily consumed' construction and the Hong Kong Cap. 132V pickled-cucumber row, and which prevents a lightly-loaded brine from diluting a result. Water content of the drained product is comparable to the fresh vegetable for cucumbers, cabbage and onions, so fresh-basis vegetable maximum levels are comparable at face value; table olives are naturally lower in moisture and carry their own sovereign rows, which are named. OUT OF SCOPE: fermented soy products, soy sauce, fish sauce and vinegar (Category 32); preserved tomato products, including canned and heat-sterilised tomatoes, passata and pickled green tomatoes (Category 32 tomato-condiments), which is why the Hong Kong heat-treated hermetically sealed tomato row at 50 ug/kg is not an anchor here; pickled fruit and chutneys whose predominant ingredient is fruit (fruit-snacks row, or Category 7 for condiment forms); pickled fish and seafood (Category 6); fermented dairy (Category 24); products marketed for ages 0 to 5 (Category 1). Where the certified presentation is a hermetically sealed tinplate can, the canned-foods tin maximum level applies as a hard stop through the tin control below. COLLAPSED SOVEREIGN SPLIT: Hong Kong sets lead at 100 ug/kg for pickled cucumbers and 400 ug/kg for table olives, MERCOSUR and Paraguay set 500 ug/kg for table olives, and Switzerland sets cadmium at 20 ug/kg for table olives with no pickled-vegetable row at all. The row binds the strictest applicable value in each cell, which means the fermented brassica products (sauerkraut, kimchi) are held to a cadmium value written for table olives and the table olives are held to a lead value written for pickled cucumbers. Splitting table olives out of this row is the recommended taxonomy fix.
pickled-fermented-vegetables.audit_scope: pickle|pickled|ferment|sauerkraut|kimchi|brine|brined|table olive|tafeloliven|\bolive|canned vegetable|preserved by heat treatment|hermetically sealed
pickled-fermented-vegetables.basis_guard: wet weight|portion ordinarily consumed|as listed|product as offered to consumer|product as placed on market|as sold|as_sold|as consumed|commodity|edible part
pickled-fermented-vegetables.basis_guard_note: Every named anchor for this row must sit in a dietary as-sold, wet-weight, edible-part or portion-ordinarily-consumed basis. The guard rejects the register's article and material bases (toy and food-contact migration, textile and leather extraction, fertiliser and growing-media dry matter, colour-additive ingredient specifications, animal-feed 12 percent moisture), any one of which would be a basis conflation if it anchored a food row. The drained-product construction is what makes the fresh-vegetable bases comparable here; brine is excluded from the analytical portion rather than averaged into it.

Pb.basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight
Pb.label: Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 9 sets lead at 100 ug/kg for pickled cucumbers specifically and for canned vegetables, and Israel MOH FCS-2016 category 20 sets 100 ug/kg for preserved vegetables; the table-olive carve-outs sit at 400 ug/kg (Hong Kong) and 500 ug/kg (MERCOSUR and Paraguay) and the Israeli preserved brassica and leafy row at 300 ug/kg.
Pb.substantiation: Hong Kong writes a pickled-cucumber lead row, so the exact cell is directly regulated for the dominant product form in this row and the cell is a government maximum level rather than a read-across. The row binds the strictest applicable value, 100 ug/kg, and the consequence is disclosed: table olives are held to a value four to five times stricter than the 400 to 500 ug/kg their own sovereign rows allow, reflecting the lye-curing and brine-contact history that those rows accommodate. HONG KONG'S OWN TREATMENT OF THE PICKLED FORM IS THE POINT OF THIS CELL: a pickled cucumber is a cucurbit fruiting vegetable, for which Hong Kong sets 50 ug/kg fresh, yet Hong Kong deliberately writes pickled cucumbers at 100 ug/kg, which is the regulator's own recognition that acidification and brine contact add a pathway the fresh value does not cover. The fresh fruiting-vegetable value is therefore not the applicable cell for this row. AUDIT DISPOSITION: the scan surfaces Hong Kong 'Tomatoes, preserved by heat treatment and hermetically sealed' at 50 ug/kg. That row governs heat-sterilised canned tomato product, not acidified, fermented or brined vegetables; preserved tomato products including canned tomatoes, passata and pickled green tomatoes route to Category 32 tomato-condiments, so the row is not applicable here. The canned-vegetable rows of Hong Kong and Israel ARE named, because canned and jarred presentations of sauerkraut and table olives are squarely in this row.

Cd.basis_label: drained product as sold, wet weight
Cd.label: Switzerland VHK 817.022.15 sets cadmium at 20 ug/kg for table olives, the only sovereign cadmium maximum level written for a product form in this row; Hong Kong Cap. 132V item 6 covers the remaining pickled and fermented vegetables through its residual vegetables row at 100 ug/kg.
Cd.substantiation: The Swiss table-olive cadmium row is not an isolated outlier: the same annex sets 20 ug/kg for fruiting vegetables, legume vegetables and pome, stone and citrus fruit, so table olives sit at the schedule's normal level for a fruit-type edible rather than at a specially strict one. Table olives are named in this taxonomy row, so 20 ug/kg is applicable to it and is the strictest applicable value. The five-fold consequence for sauerkraut, kimchi and pickled onions is disclosed, and splitting table olives into their own row is the recommended taxonomy fix.

tAs.substantiation: Direct maximum levels reaching two product forms in this row. The inorganic-arsenic read-across of 60 ug/kg is the operative arsenic constraint; total arsenic is reported for its own sake and is never satisfied by the species cell.

Israel's dried-produce inorganic-arsenic row (300 ug/kg) is not used because this row is not a dried product.

read_across.substantiation: R2 disclosed read-across from the same commodity in its fresh form, taken at face value on the comparable drained-product basis. not_material.rationale: No credible sovereign government sets a methylmercury maximum level for any fruit, vegetable or other terrestrial plant food in any jurisdiction; every methylmercury maximum level in the register is scoped to fish, shellfish and other aquatic animals, where microbial methylation in sediment and water is the documented pathway.
